dedupe_keys.name: eu coordinated risk assessment of the cybersecurity of 5g networks and the 5g toolbox 2019 to 2020

description: This risk assessment and policy case is the European Union's joint review of security risks in fifth-generation mobile networks. Following a Commission recommendation of March 2019, each Member State carried out a national risk assessment, and on 9 October 2019 the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Cooperation Group published a coordinated report that identified the main threats and threat actors (including state-backed actors), the most sensitive network assets such as core functions, network management and orchestration, the main technical and non-technical vulnerabilities, and strategic risks such as dependence on single suppliers and suppliers subject to interference from non-EU states. In January 2020 the group agreed the EU toolbox of mitigating measures for nine risk areas, including assessing the risk profile of suppliers, restricting or excluding high-risk suppliers for key assets and ensuring multi-vendor strategies, and later progress reports tracked national implementation. Coverage: the 27 EU Member States, 2019 to 2020 with follow-up reports. Format and access: free report, toolbox and Commission press releases. Caveats: the assessment is qualitative and names no suppliers; national assessments stayed confidential. Simulation uses: defining cyber-attack and supply-chain threat scenarios for telecom networks, identifying critical assets for cascading-failure models, and resilience planning of vendor diversity. Related records: ENISA's telecom security incident reports give incident statistics, and the Rogers and Optus outage reviews show core-network failures.
